findings.title: Fallback locales are not loaded on the translation path
findings.body: Fallback YAML is loaded only from ApplicationController#set_locale (I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!). I18n.translate still only calls load_locale for the current I18n.locale, and the freedom patch's load_translations no-ops unless given explicit filenames, so I18n::Backend::Fallbacks cannot load a missing fallback locale itself. Jobs, mailers, I18n.with_locale, and I18n.t(..., locale:) therefore resolve keys that are missing in the active locale as missing instead of falling back to SiteSetting.default_locale and then :en. Non-interpolated results are stored in the process-wide LRU (the getset at the cache key built just below), so a later call that does load those files still serves the cached missing or wrong string. Server-side fallbacks fail for the email and notification paths that need them, and can poison web workers that share the cache.

findings.title: Translation cache ignores the fallback locale
findings.body: Cached translations are keyed only by key, current locale, and backend object id. FallbackLocaleList now resolves missing keys using SiteSetting.default_locale, which can change at runtime and, on multisite, differs per site, but nothing includes that locale in the key or clears @cache (I18n.reload! is what nils the cache, and changing the site locale does not call it). After an admin changes the default locale, or when two sites with different default locales share a process, hot no-argument lookups keep returning the previous fallback language for the life of the size-300 LRU working set. Interpolated calls skip the cache, but most UI and email strings do not.
